spf.description: Survey of Professional Forecasters, median or mean across forecasters, one row per quarterly survey since 1968:Q4 (YEAR, QUARTER) for one variable (worksheet). Level files: VAR1 = last quarter of history, VAR2 = current-quarter nowcast, VAR3..VAR6 = the next four quarters, VARA/VARB(/C/D) = annual averages for the survey year and the following years. Growth files: dvar2..dvar6 = annualized quarter-over-quarter growth of the median (mean) level for the current and next four quarters.

file.desc: medianLevel / meanLevel (levels, and CPI/PCE inflation rates) or medianGrowth / meanGrowth (q/q annualized growth of the level forecasts; not for CPI/PCE or rates)

sheet.desc: the variable = worksheet name, case-sensitive: RGDP, NGDP, PGDP, UNEMP, EMP, CPI, CORECPI, PCE, COREPCE, TBILL, TBOND, HOUSING, INDPROD, RCONSUM, ...; long-run: CPI10, PCE10, RGDP10, CPI5YR, PCE5YR (level files only)

spf_dispersion.description: SPF cross-sectional dispersion, one row per survey (Survey_Date(T) like 2026Q3): 25th and 75th percentiles across forecasters and their difference for horizons T..T+4. measure 1 = levels (D1), 2 = q/q annualized growth (D2), 3 = 100*log(P75/P25) of levels (D3).

measure.desc: 1 levels, 2 q/q growth (annualized percentage points), 3 percent difference of levels

sheet.desc: variable worksheet, e.g. RGDP (measures 2 and 3), UNEMP, CPI, TBOND (measure 1); see source.md

spf_prob.description: SPF mean probabilities (percent) across forecasters, one row per survey: PRGDP (annual-average real GDP growth ranges), PRPGDP (GDP price inflation), PRCCPI, PRCPCE (core inflation, Q4/Q4), PRUNEMP (annual unemployment rate), RECESS (RECESS1..5 = probability of a decline in real GDP in the current and next four quarters; RECESS2 is the Anxious Index). Bin columns (PRGDP1..) are ranges whose definitions changed over time: see source.md.

greenbook.description: Federal Reserve Board staff Greenbook/Tealbook projections, one row per Greenbook (DATE = year.quarter of the Greenbook, GBdate = publication date yyyymmdd), 1967 to the last released year (5-year lag: through December 2020 as of 2026). Columns VARB4..VARB1 = history for quarters T-4..T-1, VARF0 = current quarter, VARF1..VARF9 = the next nine quarters.

sheet.desc: variable worksheet: g-prefixed = q/q annualized growth or inflation; UNEMP percent; HSTART millions of units

livingston.description: Livingston Survey (June and December since 1946), median or mean across forecasters, one row per survey (Date = Excel serial date; the pack adds survey_date). Level files: X_BP last known value, X_ZM survey month/quarter, X_6M, X_12M ahead, X_BY last annual average, X_ZY survey-year annual average, X_1Y, X_2Y following years, X_10Y 10-year average growth (RGDPX, CPI). Growth files: G_BP_To_ZM ... G_1Y_To_2Y annualized growth between those horizons.

sheet.desc: variable worksheet: RGDPX (real GDP), GDPX (nominal GDP), CPI, PPI, UNPR (unemployment), IP, TPHS (housing starts), TBILL, TBOND, PRIME, SPIF (S&P 500), BFIX, CPAT, WMFG, RTTR, AUTODF

rtdsm.description: Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists: one variable, one row per observation date (DATE like 2025:Q4 or 2025:M10) and one column per data vintage (e.g. ROUTPUT26Q3 = as published in mid-August 2026). Use it for the history the SPF forecasters saw, first releases and revisions.

file.desc: file stem: ROUTPUTQvQd (real GDP, quarterly vintages), routputMvQd (monthly vintages), NOUTPUTQvQd, PQvQd (GDP price index), pcpiMvMd (CPI), rucQvMd (unemployment rate), employMvMd (payrolls), RCONQvQd; or a catalog alias (real_gdp, cpi, unemployment ...). Other variables: the page of each variable under real-time-data-set-full-time-series-history

real_gdp.name: Real GDP (real GNP before 1992), quarterly data, quarterly vintages
real_gdp.description: Billions of chained dollars, SAAR; base year changes across vintages

real_gdp_monthly_vintages.name: Real GDP, quarterly data, monthly vintages
real_gdp_monthly_vintages.description: Each monthly vintage (advance, second, third estimates)

nominal_gdp.name: Nominal GDP, quarterly data, quarterly vintages

gdp_price_index.name: GDP price index (deflator), quarterly data, quarterly vintages
gdp_price_index.description: Index, base year changes across vintages

real_consumption.name: Real personal consumption expenditures, quarterly vintages

cpi.name: Consumer price index (CPI-U), monthly data, monthly vintages

unemployment.name: Civilian unemployment rate, monthly data, quarterly vintages

payrolls.name: Nonfarm payroll employment, monthly data, monthly vintages
